body:
As explained [here][1], this is indeed a bug/limitation. At this point it is better to wait for the new View Engine to land in v4 and then address it there (if it is still broken).

[1]: https://github.com/gkalpak/angular/commit/fe11346cae57dd7c0f4417c8c8e0cb3c07956b3f#commitcomment-20786114

I've just tested it in angular 4-rc1 and the problem is still there. According to changelog, the new view engine is already there. So maybe the next few weeks is a good time to fix this to get it into final 4.

@mhevery, is this something that we could/should support now?
(See https://github.com/gkalpak/angular/commit/fe11346cae57dd7c0f4417c8c8e0cb3c07956b3f#commitcomment-20786114 for previous discussion.)

## What is the current behavior?
I found a bug within matCheckbox. I added a disabled class to the checkbox based on a method call. When disabled, the checkbox had class disabled and therefore had grey css etc, but if it was still clicked on, it had a click event which added a disabled class to the input within the checkbox. When the disabled class was removed from the outer matCheckbox, the disabled class remained on the input, so even though the checkbox appeared not to be disabled, it couldn't accept any more input.

Issue Number: 9763


## What is the new behavior?
Clicking on a disabled checkbox should not change it in any way.

## I'm submitting a...

[ ] Other... Please describe:
## Current behavior I'm actually not sure whether this behavior is a bug or a documentation issue. I'm seeing that at some scenario described below, outputs emitted in ngOnInit are lost, but correctly processed when emitted in ngAfterViewInit. One requirement is that all components have OnPush change detection strategy. However, I'm not able to create a small reproduction example, because it always works. Basically, the scenario consists of root component and two subcomponents. The first subcomponent emits an event in ngOnInit. Root component subscribes to this output, and saves the event into a variable, which is bound as an input to the second subcomponent. But, writing a demo this way works fine. In the real-world example, it is a hybrid app. The root component is upgraded, and the hierarchy is a bit more complicated. Even when done that way, it works when the root component is visited for the first time. It breaks when ui-router destroys the root component and navigates back to it. Maybe this is just a bug somewhere (angular-upgrade, ui-router, angular core, etc.) If so and one of the requirement is using a hybrid app / upgrade, then I don't think it is worth the time fixing it / finding a reproduction scenario. But, I think that more likely it is just a documentation issue. If I understand the current documentation correctly, ngOnInit is called after inputs are initialized, but there is no word about outputs, which need not be subscribed yet. If my interpretation is correct, it would be nice that this would be emphasized in the paragraph about ngOnInit. Nevertheless, if my interpretation is not correct, then it would be nice to mention Output in the paragraph about ngOnInit too. ## Expected behavior At least, some clarification about Output and lifecycle callbacks in the documentation would be nice. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions I was unable to provide a problem demonstration, but here is a code snippet which I've created when trying to demonstrate the problem (unsuccessfully): https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-gitter-vvottn ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? Currently, I cannot find anything relevant about this topic both in official documentation, and various third-party articles, forum discussion, etc. ## Environment

Browser:
- [X] Chrome (desktop) version 67.0.3396.99

- Node version: 8.11.2
- Platform:  Linux
